text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The central bank bought gold and silver worth 500 million lei from the population over the past two months.
- Some 2,000 workers at the Avioane Craiova SA aircraft maker went on strike to protest against the plant's thin order book and to demand job security.
- Motorists in the Arad county protested against the new road tax.
ADEVARUL
- Price of bread expected to rise with some seven percent this month.
- Romania will pay back Poland communist-era debts worth $7.2 million.
- Foreign investors are interested in Romania's stock exchange.
- Bad weather has delayed sowing on some 4.7 million hectares, the paper says.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The private Dac Air airline inaugurated flights to Germany on Monday.
- Romania and the United States signed accord to allow Romania's Tarom state airline to operate flights to all U.S. airports.
- Romgas SA gas authority has to cash some 550 billion lei from its bad debtors, the paper says.
- Tarom will buy eight new Boeing 737s, the paper says.
- The Romanian Oil Company will process some 1.25 million tonnes of crude oil this month.
General:
All the papers present reactions to the signing of the Romanian-Ukrainian treaty.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The new boss of the Romanian Inteligence Service (SRI) might come from the ranks of a political party, National Peasant Party chairman Ion Diaconescu said.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Visiting Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said Italy would support Romania's bid to join NATO.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The paper presents a report on the life of street children in Bucharest.
ADEVARUL
- The paper presents the text of the Romanian-Ukrainian treaty.
- The Cluj city hall will pay for the funerals of the 15 dead babies stored in a chemical solution at a local hospital. ($=7,094 lei)
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
